Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 5) demonstrates a markedly enlarged, globular cardiac silhouette with a distinct translucent line outlining the upper mediastinum and left heart border (indicated by arrows), which represents the "varying cardiac density sign" or pericardial fat pad sign characteristic of a large pericardial effusion or haemopericardium. This radiolucent stripe separates the dense fluid-filled pericardial sac from the adjacent mediastinal structures and lung.
